target_customer: HR teams and managers at growing and distributed companies that need a searchable visual employee directory
problem: New joiners and distributed teams cannot easily see who is who, where people fit and how to reach them.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for company directories and org charts
product_category: Employee directory and org chart software

founders.name: Paul Galatis
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page: also launched 20-Over Cricket in South Africa and won a South African Music Award. The page says he built Yuppiechef; exact role not stated.

founders.name: Richard Arscott
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page with no bio; other directories name only Galatis.

competitors.name: Pingboard
competitors.what: Live org chart and company directory software
competitors.funding_then: 5M seed announced May 2018, led by Active Capital

technical_complexity.rationale: Directory and org chart UI with HR system imports; standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Data integration with HR systems gives mild stickiness, but features are easy to copy and HR suites include org charts.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; HR suites bundled directories, which limited standalone demand. Slack Fund invested instead.

market_need_then: Pingboard raised 5M in May 2018 for the same org chart and directory use case, which shows investor interest, and remote work growth made who is who tools relevant.

branding.domain_note: Uses namesandfaces.com; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, friendly product copy aimed at HR and managers

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and friendly but generic; no press or community about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Names & Faces is still active with about 20 people and claims more than 300,000 users. It raised about 3.1M in 2018 from YC, Accel, Slack Fund and Elad Gil, and no later rounds were found. It sits in a crowded niche where HR suites and Pingboard overlap, so it appears to be a small steady product rather than a breakout. No exit or shutdown was found.
notes: Funding from aggregators only: StartupList Africa 3.1M (Sep 2018), Standout lists 3.2M total; stage label not stated so recorded as other; YC page states backers Accel, YC, Slack Fund, Elad Gil. Location conflicts: YC says San Francisco, others say Cape Town and Palo Alto. The 300,000 users claim is the company's own.
